observations.flux_method_and_state: Time- and frequency-averaged Stokes-I continuum image peak; error includes fit/RMS and stated flux-scale term.; 2020-12-27; center 1.365 GHz, bandwidth 288 MHz; RACS-mid; one pulse in search

observations.epoch_band_state_and_other_notes: Accreting magnetic CV and radio LPT; Rose+26 directly confirms the CV from optical emission-line spectra and an X-ray outburst. Adopt the spectroscopic orbital period 1.368 +/- 0.053 h; the phase-connected radio recurrence period is separately 4841.89(+0.12/-0.14) s (1.34497 h) and the X-ray period is 4868 +/- 22 s. The 22.9 +/- 2.3 mJy/beam RACS-mid value is the time/frequency-averaged Stokes-I continuum-image peak, not instantaneous pulse peak flux. Rose+26 distance range is 0.4–9.1 kpc; parallax and photogeometric estimates remain separate. Gaia DR3 5946454415417964032 is the secure preferred counterpart; a neighbor 0.9 arcsec away may contaminate low-resolution photometry. Polar/asynchronous-polar/IP subtype, WD spin, WD photospheric Teff, WD mass and field, companion mass/Teff, and distance remain uncertain or model dependent. Rose+26's published UV dereddening table is superseded only by corrected inputs in the public repository; no revised peer-reviewed fit was located. See measurement ledger and ASKAP174508 review queue.

issues.competing_evidence: Rose+26 gives a broad parallax posterior 570(+620/-190) pc and a Bailer-Jones photogeometric posterior 6500(+2600/-1100) pc, then adopts 400–9100 pc; Knigge+26 v1 obtains 322(+70/-61) pc from a two-component SED. Imbrogno+26 uses 570 pc for luminosities. Gaia parallax S/N is only about 1.9 and astrometric excess noise is 3.84 mas with RUWE 1.996.
issues.why_it_matters: Luminosities, radio power, absolute magnitude and inferred system scale vary strongly with distance; the photogeometric prior may be biased by binary/accretion light.
issues.needed_action: Keep all methods and the broad range separate. Before publishing a preferred point distance or component CMD position, verify with improved astrometry or resolved component photometry; do not invert the low-S/N parallax as a precise distance.

issues.competing_evidence: Nature main text/abstract gives G=19.45+/-0.04, Methods gives 19.40+/-0.04, and Supplementary Table 1 gives 19.64+/-0.039; exact Gaia DR3 ID query gives 19.449984+/-0.039153. BP-RP=1.079 is flagged by BP/RP excess factor 2.894 and the neighbor 0.9 arcsec away.
issues.why_it_matters: A mistaken G input shifts absolute magnitude/SED scale; blended BP/RP color can misplace the system on a CMD and be mistaken for an intrinsic component color.
issues.needed_action: Use exact Gaia G as the catalog photometry value while preserving the manuscript conflict. Keep BP/RP as observed blended values and exclude them from intrinsic-color/CMD interpretation unless a resolved/deblended measurement is verified.

issues.parameter: UV extinction correction and WD temperature
issues.competing_evidence: Rose+26 published UV table has FUV/NUV=21.36/21.36 AB after the notebook multiplies observed flux by CCM89 attenuation, which dims it. The authors' 2026-07-06 public code commit adds corrected inputs FUV=18.31 and NUV=17.97 and loads that CSV in the fitting notebook; its cached blackbody output is 36460+/-7304 K, chi2_red=11.74. The published Rose fit is 26641+/-4139 K, chi2_red=4.27. Knigge+26 v1 DA SED fit gives 14500(+5000/-1200) K with different photometry/model assumptions. No formal journal correction/replacement fit was located.
issues.why_it_matters: The UV input correction materially changes the fitted hot-component temperature; none of these broad-band blackbody/SED values is a direct WD photospheric measurement.
issues.needed_action: Retain the published value and post-publication corrected-input/cached result as separate records. Before adopting a single Teff, verify whether the repository correction is author-approved as a replacement result and obtain a clean, preferably spectroscopic or UV-atmosphere analysis with deblended inputs.

issues.parameter: donor mass, temperature and evolutionary state
issues.competing_evidence: Rose+26 period-density relation gives M2=0.0963+/-0.0047 Msun (Methods rounds to 0.096+/-0.008) and empirical M6–M6.5/~2800 K; Knigge+26 v1 SED fit gives 0.052+/-0.008 Msun and ~1800 K by constraining the donor to a semi-empirical CV sequence. No donor absorption spectrum or dynamical mass is available.
issues.why_it_matters: The competing model values differ across the hydrogen-burning boundary and change conclusions about period-bouncer status and donor evolution.
issues.needed_action: Keep both model families separate and label assumptions. Resolve only with donor spectroscopy, dynamical constraints or independently validated resolved near-IR data; do not silently select the lower-error or newer estimate.

issues.competing_evidence: SOAR emission-line RVs give Porb=1.368+/-0.053 h; phase-connected radio recurrence is 4841.89(+0.12/-0.14) s; X-ray period is 4868+/-22 s. These are broadly consistent but no separate WD spin is identified. Radio cutoff modulation ~29 ks and X-ray long modulation 52+/-2 ks are distinct and poorly constrained. Rose defers polar/asynchronous-polar/IP subtype; Imbrogno discusses IP/asynchronous-polar behavior.
issues.why_it_matters: Equating recurrence/orbital/spin/beat clocks would create a false synchronization or evolutionary classification.
issues.needed_action: Retain spectroscopic Porb as the compatibility orbital value and keep each clock separately labeled. Resolve spin/subtype with long-baseline phase-resolved spectroscopy/polarimetry or a distinct stable spin signal.

issues.parameter: WD component properties and magnetic field
issues.competing_evidence: No direct WD spectrum, dynamic WD mass, cooling age, or Zeeman/cyclotron surface-field measurement was found. Rose adopts MWD=0.83+/-0.23 Msun as a CV mean; Knigge fixes 0.8 Msun. Imbrogno's kT=0.14 keV and ~1 km radius are a small accretion component. Rose's >0.96 kG is a conditional local radio-emission-region bound; its MG dipole is a chosen model.
issues.why_it_matters: Model priors, plasma temperatures and radio-emission-site fields can be mistaken for WD mass, photospheric temperature, radius or surface field.
issues.needed_action: Continue to mark these as priors/model outputs. A direct component claim needs WD-atmosphere/spectropolarimetric data and an independently constrained binary mass function.

issues.competing_evidence: Knigge+26 reports Gaussian versus Moffat PSF magnitudes differing by 0.2–0.6 mag; the neighbor is brighter and fit diagnostics show only slight elongation toward the target. Their formal errors are 0.1–0.2 mag and do not encompass this systematic; a false deblend remains possible.
issues.why_it_matters: The Ks flux drives the brown-dwarf donor mass/temperature in the SED fit.
issues.needed_action: Keep both PSF solutions with methods and uncertainties. Verify with higher-resolution resolved near-IR imaging/spectroscopy before treating Ks flux or the donor component as established.

issues.competing_evidence: Knigge+26 v1 calls the system likely post-period-minimum based on the donor-sequence-constrained SED mass; its own paper notes Porb=1.368+/-0.053 h can be pre- or post-minimum. Rose+26's Roche period-density donor estimate is above the sub-stellar boundary. The accreting magnetic-CV/LPT classification itself is secure.
issues.why_it_matters: This distinction materially changes claims about evolutionary pathways connecting CVs, WD pulsars and LPTs; the catalog must not encode a model claim as an established sequence.
issues.needed_action: Keep 'period bouncer' as a proposed model interpretation only. Do not claim a unique evolutionary pathway without an independently secure donor mass/state and comparative population evidence.
